purpose: Define the shared range result that every range composition builds on: the inclusive local-date periods of the 7-, 30-, and 90-date presets, the rolling one-year preset of 365 or 366 dates, calendar years, ISO weeks, calendar months, and custom ranges, all ending no later than a today the caller supplies; validation of the ordered daily Health Summaries given for a period; which dates have a usable value; and separate counts for dates with no summary, for every primary state, evidence condition, and publication condition, with summed coverage and a completeness flag that is never true for an incomplete range, without reading any measure's values, storing anything, or having any persistence effect.

inputs.name: today
inputs.description: The local date the caller treats as today. Every period ends on or before it. This unit never reads a clock.

inputs.name: period_request
inputs.description: A preset length of 7, 30, or 90 dates; the rolling one-year preset; a calendar year; an ISO year and week; a calendar year and month; or the first and last dates of a custom range.

inputs.name: summary_key
inputs.description: The derived measure and record type of the range, a pair from the set-source-selection-policy@1 measure vocabulary that summary-contract@1 re-exports.

inputs.name: daily_summaries
inputs.description: The daily Health Summaries of that measure and record type for dates in the period, built or decoded by summary-contract@1, in strictly ascending local-date order, each date at most once, with dates that have no summary left out.

inputs.name: publication_conditions
inputs.description: For each given daily summary, the publication conditions from the summary-contract@1 vocabulary that the caller attached when it read the summary.

outputs.name: range_period
outputs.description: An inclusive first and last local date and a period kind (last-7-dates, last-30-dates, last-90-dates, last-year, calendar-year, calendar-month, iso-week, or custom) of at most 366 dates, ending no later than today; the last-year preset runs from the day after the same date one year earlier, with 29 February read as 28 February, through today; a calendar period that contains today ends at today.

outputs.name: range_summary
outputs.description: The shared range result: the period and its date count; the dates that have a usable value, which are those whose summary is measured or partial; the dates that have no summary; counts of dates by every primary state, evidence condition, and publication condition, each name present even when its count is 0; coverage summed across the given summaries; the distinct processor and derivation versions seen; and a complete flag that is true only when every date has a measured summary with no publication condition.

outputs.name: range_failure
outputs.description: A named failure raised instead of a period or range result, carrying only its name: no date, value, identity, or bytes.

owns: the inclusive local-date periods of the presets, including the rolling one-year preset, and of calendar years, ISO weeks, calendar months, and custom ranges, their 366-date limit, and the rule that no period extends past the caller's today
validation of the daily summaries given for a range: measure, record type, period membership, order, and uniqueness
the rule that a date has a usable value exactly when its summary is measured or partial
the distinction between a date with no summary and a summary whose primary state is missing
the counts of dates by primary state, evidence condition, and publication condition, the summed coverage, and the complete flag
which failure content is free of dates, values, and identities
does_not_own: any measure's range aggregate or extra counts, such as the Steps sum, the Heart Rate sample population, Sleep durations and overlaps, or the Weight point series; the compose units do
reading or interpreting any daily summary body
the daily Health Summary, its primary-state rule, coverage, evidence conditions, and the publication-condition vocabulary; summary-contract@1 does
when a publication condition applies to a summary; operational-store, refresh-summary-state, and the completion units decide
which time zone or clock decides the local date called today, the default range, or how any period, gap, state, or condition is rendered; the presentation units do
reading the store, storing range results, or caching them
